# References {.unnumbered}

This appendix provides complete citations for all source publications used in
this teaching case, a guide to the extracted Markdown documents in the
repository, and citation language for students reporting results from the
synthetic dataset.

## Instruments and Validation Studies {.unnumbered}

The outcome instruments used in the IVAM-ED trial were validated for Brazilian
Portuguese. Key validation citations:

**SRQ-20 (Self-Reporting Questionnaire)**
Gonçalves DM, Stein AT, Kapczinski F. Performance of the self-reporting
questionnaire as a psychiatric screening questionnaire: a comparative study with
structured clinical interview for DSM-IV-TR [article in Portuguese].
*Cad Saude Publica*. 2008;24(2):380–390.

**SF-36 (36-Item Short Form Health Survey)**
Ciconelli RM, Ferraz MB, Santos W, Meinao I, Quaresma MR. Brazilian-Portuguese
version of the SF-36: a reliable and valid quality of life outcome measure.
*Rev Bras Reumatol*. 1999;39(3):143–150.

**SCI-R (Self-Care Inventory Revised)**
Teló GH, Iorra FQ, Velho BS, Sparrenberger K, Schaan BD. Validation to Brazilian
Portuguese of the Self-Care Inventory-revised for adults with type 2 diabetes.
*Arch Endocrinol Metab*. 2020;64(2):190–194.
doi:[10.20945/2359-3997000000213](https://doi.org/10.20945/2359-3997000000213)

**PSS (Perceived Stress Scale)**
Luft CDB, Sanches SdO, Mazo GZ, Andrade A. Brazilian version of the Perceived
Stress Scale: translation and validation for the elderly [article in Portuguese].
*Rev Saude Publica*. 2007;41(4):606–615.
doi:[10.1590/S0034-89102007000400015](https://doi.org/10.1590/S0034-89102007000400015)

**MMSE (Mini-Mental State Examination)**
Standard education-adjusted cutoffs used in Brazilian clinical practice:
MMSE < 24 for participants with < 5 years of education;
MMSE < 26 for participants with ≥ 5 years of education.

**CONSORT 2010 (randomized trial reporting)**
Schulz KF, Altman DG, Moher D; CONSORT Group. CONSORT 2010 statement: updated
guidelines for reporting parallel group randomised trials.
*BMJ*. 2010;340:c332.
doi:[10.1136/bmj.c332](https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.c332)

**Multiple imputation**
van Buuren S. *Flexible Imputation of Missing Data*. 2nd ed. Chapman & Hall/CRC; 2018.
Freely available online: [https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/](https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/)

van Buuren S, Groothuis-Oudshoorn K. mice: Multivariate imputation by chained
equations in R. *Journal of Statistical Software*. 2011;45(3):1–67.
doi:[10.18637/jss.v045.i03](https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v045.i03)

## Citation Language for Student Reports {.unnumbered}

When reporting results from exercises in this teaching case, use the following
language to correctly attribute the source and characterize the data:

> Analysis was performed on a synthetic dataset constructed to approximate the
> sample characteristics reported in Matzenbacher et al. (2026). The synthetic
> data were generated for teaching purposes using the simulation code in
> `R/simulate-ivam-ed.R` and do not represent individual participant data from
> the IVAM-ED trial. Full simulation documentation is available in
> `simulation-assumptions.md`.

Cite the primary publication when discussing the clinical findings:

> Matzenbacher LS, da Costa FL, de Barros LGB, et al. Interactive virtual
> assistant for health promotion among older adults with type 2 diabetes:
> the IVAM-ED randomized clinical trial. *JAMA Network Open*.
> 2026;9(1):e2553508. doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2025.53508
